subject: Private VPC delivery handoff — NetFin follow-ups
messages:
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@netfin.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC delivery handoff — NetFin follow-ups

Hi Marcus / Vanessa / Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciate the clear breakdown of hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC. NetFin is leaning toward Private VPC (customer-owned VPC with a Redwood-managed endpoint) because we need full network isolation and we want the traffic to traverse our peering/private link.

A few items we committed to share and would like your input on next steps:
- Our preference: PrivateLink endpoint or VPC peering? We are open but need guidance on which will be easier for our security team (Network + InfoSec).
- Initial CIDR ranges and a high-level diagram (attached).
- Expected throughput: ~600 reqs/min at peak, average 250 reqs/min.
- Short timeline ask: we’d like to pilot in the week of Apr 5.

Attached a simple network diagram (netfin-network-diagram.png) and our internal network contact (Carlos Ramos). Carlos will be the technical POC for routing/firewall changes.

Next steps from our side: we’ll provide the CIDRs and the security questionnaire answers by Wed 3/11. Can you confirm what specific artifacts you need from NetFin and whether Redwood prefers PrivateLink or peering for an initial pilot?

Thanks —
Aditi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private VPC delivery handoff — NetFin follow-ups

Aditi —

Great to meet you on the call. Short answers up front: either PrivateLink or VPC peering can work; PrivateLink is generally faster to operationalize for cross-account control planes (no route table changes on your side), while VPC peering can give slightly lower egress costs and direct addressability if you need internal DNS resolution to the endpoint. For most customers wanting minimal changes, we recommend PrivateLink for the pilot.

What we need from NetFin for a standard Private VPC pilot (please add Carlos if he’s not already in the thread):
- CIDR ranges for the subnets that will host the interface endpoints (allowed IPs for interface ENIs).
- IP allowlist you want Redwood to accept for management and callbacks (if any public egress is expected).
- Firewall rules / required outbound ports (we typically only require HTTPS outbound 443 to our control plane and allow inbound from PrivateLink ENIs).
- Certificate requirements: do you require mTLS for control plane or is TLS (server-only) sufficient?
- Expected qps and average/peak token counts (helps sizing).
- Desired retention/ingress S3 buckets or logs export (if you need audit copies).

I’ve attached our Private VPC preflight (redwood-private-vpc-preflight.pdf) which lists exact fields. If you can fill out the CIDR, allowlist CSV and answer cert requirements, we can provision a test endpoint in ~5 business days post-approval.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) NetFin provides CIDRs + completed preflight by Wed 3/11.
2) Redwood validates and opens a prepared PrivateLink endpoint; we run a connectivity test.
3) Pilot for 1 week, then scale to production if stable.

If you prefer VPC peering instead, we’ll need route table entries and reciprocal CIDR acceptance — that typically adds an extra 2-3 days for cloud networking teams.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Carlos and your network engineer tomorrow morning if that helps.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@netfin.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ramos <carlos@netfin.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC delivery handoff — NetFin follow-ups

Hi Aditi / Carlos —

Adding a couple of practical notes from networking ops to speed things up:
- For PrivateLink (AWS): we will ask you to create an interface endpoint in your VPC; we will provide the service name and the AZ-specific ENIs will appear in your subnets. Please provide exactly which subnets (AZs) are acceptable.
- IP allowlist: please include any NAT gateway egress IPs if your environment will egress through a public NAT for callbacks. We can also support a TLS-only flow that minimizes outbound callbacks.
- DNS: if you want internal DNS resolution to the endpoint, share the domain suffix you plan to use; we can provide a private hosted zone guidance.
- Ports: only 443 is required. We do not need additional ports opened for token traffic.

I’ve attached a quick CSV template for IP allowlist and a stub (connectivity-ip-allowlist.csv) that you can fill with the CIDRs. If you prefer peering, we’ll need to exchange account IDs and add peering acceptance steps.

If your security team requires mTLS, please flag that now — implementation will need both sides to exchange cert bundles and will add a bit more coordination.

Happy to take a 20-min walk-through with Carlos if you want to go over the diagram.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@netfin.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ramos <carlos@netfin.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC delivery handoff — NetFin follow-ups

Thanks — that’s helpful. Carlos is copied and he’ll be completing the CIDR list and IP allowlist template today. A few clarifications from our InfoSec team (answered inline):
- Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink for the pilot, agree it minimizes changes.
- mTLS: we do not require mTLS for the first pilot; TLS server-only is fine, but we will want to revisit for Prod.
- Pilot timeline: aiming for the week of Apr 5, as Marcus suggested.

Attached we’re sending our security answers (netfin-security-answers.pdf) and I’ll ask Carlos to return the filled connectivity-ip-allowlist.csv by EOD. Let us know once you’ve received the completed CSV and the preflight doc has been validated.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.
Aditi
